sources.title: DfT Statistics at DfT
facts: The latest-statistics list shows SAF and RTFO 2025 fifth provisional releases on 23 July 2026.
Vehicle licensing January to March 2026 is listed for 15 July 2026 and Transport and environment 2024 for 14 July 2026.
A statistics landing page identifies released series but does not itself create parcel-level emissions measurements.

sources.title: Ofgem BUS monthly scheme update
facts: The monthly update covers scheme activity through 30 June 2026.
Voucher applications, vouchers issued, grants paid and remaining budget are scheme-administration measures.
BUS uptake or spending must not be converted into measured greenhouse-gas reductions for an individual parcel.

sources.title: Ofgem Boiler Upgrade Scheme Product Eligibility List
facts: The Product Eligibility List was updated on 23 July 2026.
Listing on the PEL confirms specified product-standard criteria but does not guarantee all BUS eligibility requirements.
Product eligibility is not direct greenhouse-gas measurement evidence.

sources.title: DESNZ Greenhouse gas reporting conversion factors 2026
facts: The 2026 conversion factors support calculation and reporting of emissions from UK activity data.
The publication distinguishes Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 reporting uses and provides methodology and major-changes documents.
A conversion factor is not a direct measurement and requires compatible activity data and method scope.

sources.title: Ofgem BUS Guidance for Property Owners
facts: Version 5.1 is current for applications properly made on or after 28 April 2026.
Updated guidance applies uplifted eligible off-gas-grid grant values from 21 July 2026.
Eligibility and application guidance are policy-administration evidence, not measured emissions.

sources.title: Ofgem BUS Guidance for Installers
facts: Version 5.1 is current for relevant applications and includes guidance on grant values and compliance.
Uplifted eligible off-gas-grid grant values apply from 21 July 2026.
Installer guidance must not be interpreted as parcel-level emissions measurement.

sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance and tools
facts: The collection lists 2026 country-specific carbon emission factors published on 24 July 2026.
UK ETS operators may use specified inventory-derived default factors in defined monitoring and reporting circumstances.
Inventory-derived factors and compliance templates are not direct parcel emissions measurements.

sources.title: ONS UK Environmental Accounts 2026 detailed bulletin
facts: The bulletin reports 478 MtCO2e of UK greenhouse-gas emissions on a residence basis in 2024.
Residence-basis emissions include UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever their activity occurs.
Residence-basis environmental accounts must not be conflated with territorial or parcel-level emissions.

sources.title: ONS UK Environmental Accounts: 2026 latest bulletin
facts: The 2026 bulletin covers environmental accounts including emissions, direct energy use, environmental taxes and methods.
The overview states the 2024 residence-basis greenhouse-gas estimate and explains the accounting basis.
The statistical bulletin does not provide a verified binding from national accounts to individual parcels.

sources.title: ONS UK Environmental Accounts: 2026 release
facts: The release links accredited official-statistics datasets for environmental accounts.
Energy-use and atmospheric-emissions datasets retain separate definitions, classifications and tables.
Release metadata and dataset availability do not justify unsupported conversion to parcel values.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: renewable and waste sources
facts: The dataset covers UK renewable and waste energy use by source and industry from 1990 to 2024.
ONS notes that statistics may be revised as estimates, methods or systems change.
Energy-use activity data are not equivalent to measured greenhouse-gas emissions for a parcel.

sources.title: DESNZ Conversion factors 2026 Code statement
facts: The statement addresses trustworthiness, quality and value under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
The conversion-factor product is published annually by the DESNZ greenhouse-gas inventory team.
Quality assurance of a factor product does not change factor-versus-measurement semantics.

sources.title: Ofgem Boiler Upgrade Scheme
facts: BUS operates in England and Wales and provides grants for eligible low-carbon heating technologies.
The current scheme page lists an uplifted £9,000 category for specified eligible off-gas-grid heat-pump installations from 21 July 2026 to 31 March 2027.
Grant values and scheme scope are not measured greenhouse-gas savings.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: total
facts: The dataset covers direct and reallocated UK energy use by industry from 1990 to 2024.
ONS revision guidance distinguishes planned revisions from genuine corrections.
Energy-use totals must not be assigned to parcels without a separate verified binding method.

sources.title: DfT forthcoming publications
facts: The page lists future publication dates including the final 2025 SAF Mandate report in November 2026.
Future scheduled publications are metadata about planned releases rather than observed statistics.
No future release is treated as available evidence before its publication date.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: fossil fuels by fuel type and industry
facts: The dataset covers fossil-fuel use by industry and fuel type from 1990 to 2024.
The page preserves scheduled revision and correction history, including a 2026 correction entry.
Fuel-use data require compatible factors and methods before any emissions calculation and do not directly bind to parcels.

sources.title: DESNZ BUS approved grant categories and values notice
facts: The current notice is effective from 21 July 2026 and applies to England and Wales.
The notice defines approved grant categories and values under the BUS regulations.
Approved grant values are regulatory-policy data rather than measured emissions or carbon savings.

sources.title: DESNZ BUS regulations approved standards and grants collection
facts: The collection was last updated on 21 July 2026 and links current approved standards, categories and grant levels.
Earlier grant-category versions were superseded by the current version from 21 July 2026.
Regulatory standards and grant levels must retain effective dates and are not emissions observations.

sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS detailed guidance
facts: The guidance covers installations, aviation, maritime, permitting, monitoring, reporting, verification and registry obligations.
Domestic maritime scope applies from 1 July 2026 with specified reporting and allowance-surrender obligations.
Compliance obligations and surrender quantities must not be equated with parcel physical-emissions measurements.

sources.title: Taking part in UK ETS markets
facts: The markets guidance was updated on 10 July 2026 with latest Cost Containment Mechanism figures.
The revised 2026 auction calendar reflects maritime inclusion and UK allowance market arrangements.
Allowance prices, auction volumes and market activity are not physical greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS Public Reports registry
facts: The registry public-reports page provides 2026 installation-operator account-holder and allocation reports published 5 July 2026.
Registry reports contain account and allocation information under the UK ETS registry framework.
Free allocation or account information is not a parcel emissions measurement.

sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS collection
facts: The collection states that the UK ETS replaced UK participation in the EU ETS from 1 January 2021.
The page was updated 1 July 2026 with 2026 participation guidance.
Scheme coverage and participation rules are policy/compliance evidence rather than parcel emissions observations.

sources.title: DESNZ UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions 2005 to 2024
facts: The publication provides UK local-authority and regional greenhouse-gas estimates for 2005 to 2024.
The page links statistical-release, data-table and technical-report products and was updated 30 June 2026.
Local-authority estimates retain their defined methodology and geography and are not individual parcel measurements.

sources.title: NAEI Greenhouse Gas Emissions Data
facts: The page lists the 2026 UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory covering 1990 to 2024 and related inventory products.
It also lists point-source, gridded and interactive-map products with publication-year and next-publication metadata.
A listed future or seasonal publication date does not prove that a newer point-source or gridded dataset has already been released.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve publication/update date.
Preserve the source reference period.
Keep provisional, final and current statuses distinct.
Preserve UK, GB, England/Wales, local-authority and other geography scope.
Keep residence, territorial, end-user and other accounting bases distinct.
Do not treat activity or energy-use data as measured emissions.
Do not treat emission factors as direct measurements.
Do not treat grants, vouchers or eligibility as emissions measurement.
Keep policy, guidance and regulation separate from observations.
Keep allowances, prices and allocations separate from physical emissions.
Do not map facility or operator evidence to a parcel without verified binding.
Do not assign local-authority aggregates to individual parcels.
Future releases remain future metadata until published.
Preserve source units and do not silently convert.
Preserve denominators for intensity, rate and share metrics.
Preserve methodology version, revision and correction history.
Require compatible activity data, factors and method before conversion.
Do not infer an individual parcel greenhouse-gas value.
Retain corrections and superseded-version metadata.
Require explicit QA review before PASS.
